mainTopic: Public paths through private fields: why the owner cannot swap or reclaim them, acquiring a path by walking, and the standard widths of paths
overview: This amud continues the משנה about an owner who moves a public path from the middle of his field to the side. רב אשי explains why the owner never gets the old path back: any side path is a winding route, closer for some people and farther for others. The גמרא then asks why the owner cannot take back the new path he gave. It answers that the משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who holds that a path the public chooses for itself is theirs. רב גידל in the name of רב limits this to a path that was lost in that field. A different report of רב rules against רבי אליעזר, and under that view the reason is רב יהודה's rule that a strip the public has taken over may not be ruined. The גמרא explains that for רבי אליעזר walking acquires land, based on ה׳ telling אברהם to walk the land. חכמים reject that proof, but they agree that a path through vineyards is acquired by walking. The amud ends with the widths of paths: a vineyard path, a private path (four cubits, which is the same as a loaded donkey's width), a road between cities (eight cubits), and a public road (sixteen cubits).

steps.title: רב אשי: every side path is a winding route
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains why the owner does not get his original path back: any side path counts as a דרך עקלתון, closer for some people and farther for others.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Any path on the side counts as a winding route. It is closer for this person and farther for that person.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives his explanation for the משנה's rule that the owner does not get his original middle path back after giving the public a side path.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original path went straight through the field. Any new path along the edge helps some travelers and makes the trip longer for others. Since it always hurts somebody, the owner can never force the public to give up the original path in exchange.

keyTerms.meaning: On the side, meaning a path moved to the edge of the field
A crooked or winding route
Closer for one person and farther for another

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Any path on the side
is a winding route;
it is close for this one, and far for that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues earlier explanations from before this section of why the owner's original path is not returned to him.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reasoning: a side path always disadvantages someone
steps.terutzMaskana: The public can never be made to give up the straight original path for a side path.
steps.whyThisMatters: It makes the rule general: the owner never gets the old path back, even when the new side path seems just as good.

steps.title: Why can't the owner take back the new path he gave?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why, under the משנה's rule that the gift stays given, the owner cannot say: take back your old path and return my new one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him say to them: Take your path, and give me mine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other half of the משנה, which says that whatever path the owner gave stays given. It asks why the owner cannot just undo the swap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The public now uses both paths. The owner could argue: you keep your original public path and I take back the land I gave you, so nobody loses anything. The question is why the משנה does not allow this.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him say to them, a formula for suggesting an obvious argument
Take yours
Give me mine

phrases.english: But let him say to them:
Take yours
phrases.notes: "Yours" means the original public path through the middle of the field.

phrases.english: and give me mine!
phrases.notes: "Mine" means the side path he gave them, which was originally his own land.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא לְהוּ שִׁקְלוּ דִּידְכוּ וְהַבוּ לִי דִּידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the owner's original path to the new path he handed over.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that what the owner gave stays given
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the public gets its old path back, it loses nothing. So why should the owner lose the land he gave?

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי אליעזר: a path the public chose is theirs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who holds in a ברייתא that when the public chooses a path for itself, it keeps it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי אליעזר's. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי אליעזר: If the public chose a path for themselves, what they chose, they chose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by identifying the author of the משנה as רבי אליעזר, and it brings a ברייתא showing his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that once the public has chosen a path through a field, it becomes theirs. So once the public accepted and used the side path, it became a public path that the owner cannot take back. That is why the משנה says that what he gave stays given.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? A formula for naming the author of a source
The public, many people together
Who chose or selected

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
It is Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
The public that chose a path for themselves,
what they chose, they chose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzMaskana: Under רבי אליעזר, a path the public selected becomes theirs, so the gifted side path stays public.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule that the gift stays given is explained as following רבי אליעזר: a path the public chooses for itself belongs to the public.

steps.title: Does רבי אליעזר let the public steal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's view: how can the public just take a path through someone's private field?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אליעזר, is the public a band of robbers?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא it just quoted. It seems to let the public take private land without permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken at face value, רבי אליעזר's rule lets many people take over a private field just because they chose to walk there. That looks like plain robbery, so the גמרא asks how it can be correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Robbers, people who take property by force
Are they?

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Eliezer,
are the public robbers?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא brought in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's rule that a path the public chooses stays theirs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking a path through private land without the owner's permission would be stealing. Being many people does not give them the right to steal.

steps.title: רב גידל: the case is a path that got lost in that field
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל in the name of רב explains that רבי אליעזר only means a case where the public already had a path in that field but its exact location was lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: For example, where they lost a path in that field.
steps.whatsHappening: רב גידל answers the robbery challenge by narrowing רבי אליעזר's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The public already owned a path through this field, but nobody knows anymore exactly where it ran. In that case the public is not stealing. It is choosing where its own existing right of way goes, so whatever it chooses stands.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, such as; here it limits the case
That was lost
In that same field

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
For example, where a path was lost to them
in that field.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב כְּגוֹן שֶׁאָבְדָה לָהֶן דֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the robbery challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי אליעזר lets the public grab any path through any field.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר only speaks about a field where the public already had a path that got lost, so no robbery is involved.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר is not saying the public may take new land. The public already had a right of way there; only its exact spot was forgotten.

steps.title: Then why does רב rule against רבי אליעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if רבי אליעזר's view is this reasonable, why does רבה בר רב הונא report that רב ruled the הלכה does not follow him?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why did רבה בר רב הונא say in the name of רב: The הלכה does not follow רבי אליעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a contradiction between two reports in the name of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב גידל's explanation makes רבי אליעזר sound completely fair: the public is only finding its own lost path. But רבה בר רב הונא quotes רב as rejecting רבי אליעזר. Why would רב reject a view that he himself explained so sensibly?

keyTerms.meaning: If so, a formula for pushing a previous answer to a problem
Why?
The practical law does not follow this view

phrases.english: If so, why

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: did Rabba bar Rav Huna say that Rav said:
The halakha is not like Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי אַמַּאי אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 5 as the basis for a new challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling, quoted in רב's name, that the הלכה does not follow רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once רבי אליעזר is limited to a lost path, his view is obviously fair, so it makes no sense for רב to rule against it.

steps.title: Two different reports of what רב said
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two statements in רב's name come from different students who reported רב differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who teaches this does not teach that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying the two quotes of רב come from two different reports that disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One report, רב גידל's, has רב explaining רבי אליעזר as a case of a lost path. The other report, רבה בר רב הונא's, has רב ruling against רבי אליעזר. Each student would not accept the other's version, so there is no contradiction inside one report.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who teaches this statement
Does not teach that statement

phrases.english: The one who teaches this
phrases.notes: "This" is רב גידל's quote of רב, explaining the case as a lost path.

phrases.english: does not teach that.
phrases.notes: "That" is רבה בר רב הונא's quote of רב, that the הלכה does not follow רבי אליעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי הָא לָא מַתְנֵי הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two conflicting reports of the same אמורא
steps.terutzMaskana: There is a disagreement about what רב actually said. One version explains רבי אליעזר, and the other rejects him.
steps.whatToRemember: When two statements in the same אמורא's name clash, the גמרא can answer "מאן דמתני הא לא מתני הא": they are two different reports, not one consistent position.

steps.title: Why can't the owner take back the path he gave?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason the field owner cannot reclaim the path he gave the public, according to the view that the הלכה does not follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step. According to רבה בר רב הונא, who says the הלכה is not like רבי אליעזר, why does the owner lose the path he gave the public?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 showed that one report of רב rejects רבי אליעזר's view. So the reason for the ruling in the משנה cannot be רבי אליעזר's rule that the public keeps a path it picked. The גמרא now needs a different reason for why the owner cannot take back the path he himself gave.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the reason?

phrases.english: And what is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: for רבה בר רב הונא, who rules against רבי אליעזר, why can't the owner take back the path he gave?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 7's conclusion that one tradition of רב rejects רבי אליעזר, so a new reason is needed for the משנה's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The legal reason the owner cannot reclaim the path he gave the public, without relying on רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Because of רב יהודה's rule about a public border strip
steps.stepSummary: The reason is רב יהודה's rule that a border strip the public has taken possession of may not be ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of רב יהודה, for רב יהודה said: A border strip that the public has taken possession of may not be ruined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a rule from רב יהודה: once the public has started using a strip of land as a path, no one may ruin it or take it away from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a border strip that the public simply started using is protected, then a path the owner actually handed over to the public is surely protected. So the owner cannot take it back, even without רבי אליעזר's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A border strip of land between fields
The public took possession of it, by using it as a path
It is forbidden to ruin it

steps.whyThisMatters: רב יהודה's rule is a key principle: once the public has established use of a path, that use is protected.

phrases.english: Because of the statement of Rav Yehuda –
as Rav Yehuda said:
A border strip that the public took possession of –
it is forbidden to ruin it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יהודה's rule that a public-used border strip may not be ruined. This applies all the more to a path the owner gave to the public.

steps.title: How does the public acquire the path according to רבי אליעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what act of acquisition lets the public acquire the path it chose, according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי אליעזר, by what means does the public acquire it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי אליעזר's view that the public keeps a path it picked. It asks what act actually makes the path theirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, land is acquired through a real act of acquisition. The public just walked on the path, so the גמרא wants to know what legal action made it theirs.

keyTerms.meaning: By what means did they acquire?
The public

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Eliezer –
by what means does the public acquire it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר רַבִּים בְּמַאי קָנוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי אליעזר's view from steps 3 and 5 and asks how the acquisition works.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The act of acquisition through which the public gains the path according to רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Walking acquires: the ברייתא of רבי אליעזר and חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The public acquires by walking, because רבי אליעזר holds in a ברייתא that walking along a field's length and width acquires it. חכמים disagree and say walking does nothing without a real act of taking possession.
steps.simpleTranslation: By walking. As a ברייתא teaches: If one walked along its length and its width, he acquires the place he walked. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. And חכמים say: Walking does not help at all until he takes possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the public acquires by walking (הילוך). It brings a ברייתא showing that רבי אליעזר holds walking is an act of acquisition, while חכמים say it is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, walking through land counts as an act of acquisition. So the public, by walking on the path, made it theirs. חכמים say walking alone is not enough; a person needs a proper act of taking possession (חזקה).

keyTerms.meaning: Walking, here meaning walking through land as a way to acquire it
Along its length and its width
That he takes possession with a proper act of acquisition (חזקה)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: walking acquires land. חכמים: walking does not acquire, a real act of possession is needed.

phrases.english: By walking.
As it is taught in a baraita: If one walked in it along its length and its width –
he acquired the place where he walked,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
And the Sages say:
walking does not help at all,
until he takes possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 and supports the answer with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The public acquires by walking, since רבי אליעזר holds walking is a valid act of acquisition.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's source: אברהם walking the land
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that רבי אליעזר learns walking acquires from the פסוק where ה׳ tells אברהם to walk the land's length and width, because He will give it to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: What is the reason of רבי אליעזר? As it is written: "Arise, walk through the land, its length and its width, for I will give it to you."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives the source for רבי אליעזר's view that walking acquires land. The source is a פסוק about אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ told אברהם to walk the length and width of ארץ ישראל, and right after that said "for I will give it to you." רבי אליעזר reads this to mean the walking itself was the way of acquiring the land. The words "length and width" match the wording of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Arise, walk through the land
For I will give it to you
What is the reason/source?

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said,
what is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?
phrases.notes: Careful: רבי אלעזר, who is speaking, is a different person from רבי אליעזר, whose view he explains.

phrases.english: As it is written: "Arise, walk through the land
its length and its width,
for I will give it to you."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source in the תורה for רבי אליעזר's position from the ברייתא in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's rule that walking along the length and width of land acquires it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 13:17: ה׳ tells אברהם to walk the land's length and width, "for I will give it to you."

steps.title: How חכמים read the פסוק about אברהם
steps.stepSummary: חכמים say the walking in the פסוק was not an act of acquisition. ה׳ told אברהם to walk out of love for him, so that it would be easy for his children to conquer the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן: There, it was because of ה׳'s love for אברהם that He told him this, so that it would be easy to conquer before his children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how חכמים deal with רבי אליעזר's פסוק. They say אברהם's walk had a special purpose and was not a legal way of acquiring land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים agree the פסוק says to walk, but they say the walking did not make a legal acquisition. It was a special favor out of love for אברהם, to make the later conquest easy for his descendants. So the פסוק teaches nothing about the general laws of buying land.

keyTerms.meaning: The love (ה׳ had) for אברהם
Easy to conquer
The Sages (the same as חכמים in the ברייתא)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis –
there, it was because of the love for Abraham
that He said this to him,
so that it would be easy to conquer
before his children.
phrases.notes: Meaning his descendants would have an easy time conquering the land later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how חכמים reject the proof from the פסוק brought in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the פסוק about אברהם as a source that walking acquires land in general.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The walking in the פסוק had a special purpose, love for אברהם and an easy conquest for his descendants. It was not an ordinary legal acquisition.

steps.title: חכמים agree for a path through vineyards
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר that a path through vineyards is acquired by walking, since it was made for walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר about a path through vineyards. Since it was made for walking, it is acquired by walking.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא adds a case where even חכמים agree that walking acquires: a path through vineyards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים usually say walking does not acquire land. But a path is made only for walking, so walking on it is the natural way of using it, and that use counts as taking possession. This is an exception within חכמים' rule, not a change in their general view.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages agree
A path through vineyards
Since it was made for walking

steps.whatToRemember: Even חכמים agree that a path through vineyards, which is made for walking, can be acquired by walking.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean חכמים changed their mind about fields in general. They still say walking does not acquire a field. Only a path, whose whole use is walking, is acquired this way.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:
The Sages agree with Rabbi Eliezer
regarding a path through vineyards,
since it was made for walking –
it is acquired by walking.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוֹדִים חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁל כְּרָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the מחלוקת from step 11 by giving a case where חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A path through vineyards, being made for walking, is acquired by walking, even according to חכמים.

steps.title: רב יצחק בר אמי sets the width of a vineyard path
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אמי rules that a vineyard path must be wide enough to carry a bundle of vine branches and turn around.
steps.simpleTranslation: When people came before רב יצחק בר אמי, he told them: Give him a path wide enough to carry a load of vine branches and turn around.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a court case over how wide a path through a vineyard must be. רב יצחק בר אמי gives a practical measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 discussed a path through vineyards. Now the question is how wide such a path is. The measure is practical: wide enough to do vineyard work, like carrying a bundle of cut branches and turning around with it.

keyTerms.meaning: A load or bundle
Vine branches (cut shoots from the vines)
Turns around

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: When they came before Rav Yitzchak bar Ami,
he said to them: Give him a path

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּדָרֵי טוּנָא דִשְׁבִישָׁתָא וְהָדַר.
phrases.english: wide enough that he can carry a load of vine branches and turn around.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how a vineyard path is acquired to how wide it must be.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vineyard path must be wide enough to carry a bundle of vine branches and turn around.

steps.title: The wide measure applies only when fences close in the path
steps.stepSummary: The wide measure applies only when fences close in the path. Without fences, the path only has to be wide enough to walk.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this where fences close in the path. But where fences do not close it in, it only has to be wide enough to lift one foot and put down the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits רב יצחק בר אמי's ruling. The wide measure is needed only when fences on both sides close in the path.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With fences on both sides, a wide bundle would get stuck, so the path itself must be wide. With no fences, the bundle can stick out over the sides. So the path only has to fit a person's steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Fences close in the path on its sides
Lifts a foot and puts down a foot (just walking space)

phrases.english: And we said this only where fences close in the path,
but where fences do not close it in,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּשָׁקֵיל כַּרְעָא וּמַנַּח כַּרְעָא.
phrases.english: it only needs to be wide enough to lift one foot and put down the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of step 15 to a path with fences on its sides.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fenced path: wide enough for a load of branches. Unfenced path: just walking width.
steps.whatToRemember: The width of a vineyard path depends on whether fences close it in. With fences, it must fit a load of branches. Without fences, it only needs room to walk.

steps.title: אחרים measure a private path by a loaded donkey
steps.stepSummary: After the משנה's 'four cubits' for a private path, a ברייתא brings אחרים: wide enough for a loaded donkey. רב הונא rules like them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says a private path is four cubits. A ברייתא teaches that אחרים say it is wide enough for a donkey to pass with its load. רב הונא says the הלכה follows אחרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's measure for a private path. Then it brings a ברייתא with a different way to measure it, and רב הונא rules on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a number, אחרים give a practical test: the path must let a loaded donkey through. רב הונא rules like אחרים. This ruling becomes important in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A private path belonging to an individual
'Others': a name for a תנא whose name the ברייתא does not give
With its load

phrases.english: A private path is four cubits.
It was taught: Others say:
wide enough for a donkey to pass with its load.
Rav Huna said: The halacha follows the Others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה and its next topic, the private path.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A private path must be wide enough for a loaded donkey, and the הלכה follows אחרים.

steps.title: דייני גולה give two and a half cubits
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says דייני גולה measure a private path at two and a half cubits. רב הונא rules like them too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: דייני גולה say two and a half cubits. And רב הונא said: The הלכה follows דייני גולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא with an exact number for the private path. רב הונא rules like this view too. This sets up the problem in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רב הונא seems to have two rulings: one following אחרים, and one following דייני גולה. That sounds like he ruled for two different opinions, which the גמרא will question.

keyTerms.meaning: The judges of the exile (judges in בבל)
Cubits (another word for אמות)

phrases.english: And another baraita teaches:

phrases.aramaic: דַּיָּינֵי גוֹלָה אוֹמְרִים: שְׁנֵי גַמָּדִים וּמֶחֱצָה.
phrases.english: The judges of the exile say: two and a half cubits.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הֲלָכָה כְּדַיָּינֵי גוֹלָה.
phrases.english: And Rav Huna said: The halacha follows the judges of the exile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ברייתא and a second ruling of רב הונא on the same question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A private path is two and a half cubits, and the הלכה follows דייני גולה.

steps.title: רב הונא seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב הונא can rule like דייני גולה when he already ruled like אחרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב הונא say the הלכה follows אחרים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא. He seems to rule like two different opinions on the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two rulings on one question should not point to two different opinions. If אחרים and דייני גולה disagree, רב הונא cannot follow both.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (introduces a contradiction)

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Huna say: The halacha follows the Others!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets רב הונא's ruling in step 18 against his ruling in step 17.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He cannot follow two different opinions on the same measurement.

steps.title: Both opinions describe the same width
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a loaded donkey's width and two and a half cubits are the same measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one and that one are the same measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no contradiction. The two views do not disagree at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחרים describe the width by its use, a loaded donkey. דייני גולה give the number for that same width, two and a half cubits. So רב הונא is ruling on one measure, described in two ways.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one
One measure

phrases.english: This and that are one and the same measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two opinions are the same (no real disagreement)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אחרים and דייני גולה give two different widths.
steps.terutzMaskana: A loaded donkey needs two and a half cubits, so both views describe the same width.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא rules like both אחרים and דייני גולה because a loaded donkey's width is two and a half cubits.

steps.title: A road between cities is eight cubits
steps.stepSummary: After the משנה's sixteen cubits for a public road, a ברייתא adds that a road between cities is eight cubits.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says a public road is sixteen cubits. The רבנן taught: a private path is four cubits, and a road from city to city is eight cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's measure for a public road. Then it brings a ברייתא that adds a middle kind of road.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Between the private path (four cubits) and the public road (sixteen cubits), the ברייתא adds a third kind: a road that links two cities, which is eight cubits wide.

keyTerms.meaning: A public road
A road from one city to another

phrases.english: A public road is sixteen cubits.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: דֶּרֶךְ הַיָּחִיד – אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: A private path is four cubits.
A road from city to city is eight cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the משנה's next measure, the public road, and brings a ברייתא with more categories.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Private path: four cubits. Road between cities: eight cubits. Public road: sixteen cubits.
